''See also: [[Dragon's Fang Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[dragons|Dragon]]'s Fangs are a collection of thirteen specialized weapons forged by the The Wanderer{{!}}Wanderer, also known as [[Valin]], to serve his original [[Dragon Army]]. These weapons act as keys to the territory of [[Valinhall]] and allow its [[Travelers]] to manifest power within themselves rather than summoning external forces. [[Forged]] from nearly indestructible [[Tartarus steel]], the Fangs are capable of slicing through [[stone]], trees, and heavy armor. While some blades possess unique characteristics—such as being gold-lined or having pitted, chipped surfaces—they all share the ability to be summoned by their designated wielders. A [[Valinhall Travelers|Valinhall Traveler]] can summon a [[Fang]] from [[the House]] while in the outside world, though [[Travelers]] located within [[the House]] cannot summon weapons from external locations. The Fangs are highly significant to the stability and power of [[Valinhall]]; many have been lost over time, and their recovery is a primary objective for the [[Nye Eldest]]. Notable examples include [[Mithra]], the final and longest [[sword]] forged by [[Valin]], and [[Seijan]], the tenth [[Fang]]. The weapons are sometimes described as having a level of independent thought.}}

== House of Blades ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|The [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]] is a [[sword]] forged by the [[The Wanderer|Wanderer]] and bestowed upon the twelve original soldiers of the [[Dragon Army]]. While thirteen such weapons were originally created, only four remain active in the current era. These blades possess the unique ability to be summoned by a wielder who has earned their respect. During his trials, which are designed to test the physical strength required to wield such a weapon, [[Simon]] carries an undersized replica from the [[Valinhall armory]]. He demonstrated significant skill when he used this replica to slice through [[Erastes]]' bonds with an ease comparable to a true [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]].}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|Only four of the thirteen swords ([[Dragon's Fang|Dragon's Fangs]]) remain in use.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c9" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|Only four of the thirteen [[Dragon's Fang|Dragon's Fangs]] are currently active.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c10">''House of Blades'', chapter 10</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|A [[Dragon's Fang]] is a weapon that can be summoned if its respect has been earned.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c10" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|[[Simon]] carries an undersized replica of a [[Dragon's Fang]] from the [[Valinhall armory]].<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c11">''House of Blades'', chapter 11</ref>}}</li>

</ul></div>

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|[[Forged]] by the [[The Wanderer|Wanderer]] from [[Tartarus steel]], [[dragons|Dragon]]'s Fangs are gracefully curving swords that serve as lost artifacts. These weapons are used by various individuals, including [[Kai]], [[Indirial]], [[Denner Weeks|Denner]], and [[Simon]], while [[Andra Agnos|Andra]] carries one buckled to her belt. A [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]] can assist in opening a Gate, facilitate easier travel to [[the House]], and is a burden that only a chosen daughter can bear. During combat, the clashing of these blades produces an ear-shattering noise, and it is noted that the thirteenth [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]] has an heir.}}

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|A [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]] is a [[Mithra]] classification for [[Valinhall]]-forged swords that feature a smooth vein of gold running down the flat of the blade. These thirteen sentient weapons are capable of cutting through [[stone]] walls, [[chains]], and trees, possessing enough power to penetrate an [[Incarnation]]'s rib cage or split [[Alin]]'s armor. While some blades shine mirror-bright and others are spattered with black spots like ink, the gold-and-silver weapon of [[Valin|Valin the Wanderer]] is among them. Throughout various conflicts, these artifacts have been held by individuals such as [[Simon]], [[Indirial]], [[Andra Agnos|Andra]], and [[Kai]], or even taken hostage and held by [[Kathrin]]. During his journey, [[Simon]] struggled with the weight of a blade he was too weak to lift before eventually using his [[dragons|Dragon]]'s [[Fang]] to strike [[Asphodel]]'s neck.}}
